notes.constructors: Means and medians over the scenarios that survive the integrity filter. Every constructor faced the identical demand realization within each scenario and contributes the same {runs_per} runs: the scenario cells containing the degenerate runs of Table~\ref{{tab:excluded}} were dropped for all constructors, not only for the one that failed them, so no constructor is averaged over a subset that flatters it. Medians are reported alongside means because a single extreme scenario can move a mean substantially at this sample size. Lost (kg) reports mean cumulative discarded mass per run; it is distinct from overflow bin-days.
notes.strategies: LM-CF70/LM-CF90 are Last-Minute critical-fill thresholds of 70\% and 90\%; SL1/SL2 are Service-Level projection horizons of one and two days. Restricted to the slices shared by all five variants so that the marginal means are comparable: the excluded runs of Table~\ref{tab:excluded} removed the study's hardest scenario cell from Look-Ahead and Service-Level (SL2) but not from the other three variants, which would otherwise have flattered them. Medians are reported alongside means. Lost (kg) reports mean cumulative discarded mass per run; it is distinct from overflow bin-days.
notes.improvers: Each pair has the same constructor, strategy, region and demand realization, with a different configured improver. This is not a controlled improver treatment: upstream constructor outcomes also differ in some pairs, so the deltas are descriptive associations rather than causal effects. Win counts exclude ties, which are reported separately. Waste lost is cumulative discarded mass per run.
notes.horizon: The 90-day archive is a selected, non-factorial subset; its selection rule is pending recovery of the run records, and Pareto-only carry-forward is not established (Sect.~\ref{sec:provenance}). Configurations are compared against themselves across horizons, not used to rank constructors at 90 days. The paired values describe this selected subset and do not estimate a horizon effect for the full factorial design. Lost (kg) reports mean cumulative discarded mass per run; it is distinct from overflow bin-days.
notes.scenarios: The demand rows use the 216 policy slices present under both processes; the network rows use the 136 policy slices present on all three networks. Balancing prevents exclusions confined to Gamma-3 at $N=350$ from making the remaining levels look artificially better or worse. Lost (kg) reports mean cumulative discarded mass per run; it is distinct from overflow bin-days.
notes.excluded: $D$ is the horizon in days and ``FF 350'' the Figueira da Foz network at $N=350$. Runs below their scenario median by more than {threshold}\% are excluded. The three 30-day logs contain all 30 daily records but last collect on days 16, 16 and 22; later full bins keep contributing overflow events. The 90-day raw log is pending recovery, so its termination and last collection day are not established. These are anomalous policy outputs; neither a crash nor truncated logging follows from the tonnage gap alone. Lost (kg) is the cumulative discarded mass in each excluded run.
